title: La fritanga
desc: Dinner comes off a grill on the sidewalk

sn.s: En la noche hay humo en la calle.
sn.e: At night there is smoke in the street.
The smoke smells of meat.

sn.s: El humo viene de la esquina.
sn.e: The smoke comes from the corner.

sn.s: En la esquina hay una fritanga.
sn.e: On the corner there is a fritanga.

sn.s: Una fritanga es una parrilla en la calle.
sn.e: A fritanga is a grill in the street.

sn.s: La fritanga se pone cuando cae el sol.
sn.e: The fritanga is set up when the sun goes down.

sn.s: La fritanga es de doña Marta.
sn.e: The fritanga belongs to doña Marta.

sn.s: Doña Marta pone la parrilla a las cinco.
sn.e: Doña Marta sets up the grill at five.

sn.s: A las seis ya hay fila.
sn.e: By six there is already a queue.

sn.s: La fila llega hasta la otra casa.
sn.e: The queue reaches as far as the next house.

sn.s: Yo me pongo en la fila.
sn.e: I join the queue.
I look at what there is.

sn.s: Hay carne asada en la parrilla.
sn.e: There is grilled meat on the grill.
There are green plantain crisps.

sn.s: Hay maduro frito, dulce y suave.
sn.e: There is fried ripe plantain, sweet and soft.
There is gallo pinto, always.

sn.s: Hay queso frito y hay pollo.
sn.e: There is fried cheese and there is chicken.
There is cabbage salad.
I do not know how to order yet.

sn.s: Miro a la señora de adelante.
sn.e: I watch the woman in front.
"Give me meat with tajadas," she says.
Then it is my turn.
"Buenas," I say.
"Buenas. What can I serve you?" doña Marta says.
"Give me meat with tajadas, please."
"With gallo pinto?"
"Yes, with gallo pinto."
"And maduro?"
"Maduro as well," I say.

sn.s: Doña Marta sirve todo en una hoja.
sn.e: Doña Marta serves it all on a leaf.

sn.s: La hoja es de plátano, verde y grande.
sn.e: The leaf is a plantain leaf, green and big.
There is no plate.
The leaf is the plate.

sn.s: Pone la carne en la hoja.
sn.e: She puts the meat on the leaf.
She puts the tajadas on top.
She puts the maduro to one side.

sn.s: Pone el gallo pinto y el queso.
sn.e: She puts the gallo pinto and the cheese.
Then she folds the leaf.

sn.s: Me da todo caliente en la mano.
sn.e: She hands me the lot, hot.
"That's sixty," she says.
I pay her sixty pesos.
It is cheap for that much food.

sn.s: Me como todo de pie en la calle.
sn.e: I eat the lot standing in the street.

sn.s: Nadie se sienta en la fritanga.
sn.e: Nobody sits down at a fritanga.

sn.s: Uno come de pie y habla.
sn.e: You eat standing up and you talk.
The meat is good.

sn.s: Las tajadas están saladas y duras.
sn.e: The tajadas are salty and crisp.
The maduro is sweet.
All of it together is very good.

sn.s: Roberto llega y se pone en la fila.
sn.e: Roberto arrives and joins the queue.
"What did you order?" he asks me.
"Meat with tajadas and maduro."
"Good," he says. "You've learned."

sn.s: Cada noche paso por la fritanga.
sn.e: Every night I go past the fritanga.

sn.s: Cada noche hay humo y hay fila.
sn.e: Every night there is smoke and a queue.

sn.s: Y doña Marta ya sabe lo que pido.
sn.e: And doña Marta already knows what I order.
